title: Lãi suất 4,35%: cần biết trước 29/9

subtitles.text: Since the start of 2026, Australia's cash rate has risen three times, from 3.6 to 4.35 percent.
Up 0.25 percent in February, March and May, then held in June and August.
Inflation is the main reason: the RBA says it's still too high, not back mid-target until late 2027.
Example: a $600,000, 30-year loan pays almost $290 more a month, if passed on in full.
The RBA also said it could raise rates further if inflation risks grow.
The next decision is announced on Tuesday, 29 September.
Want to know how this affects your loan? Message Finance Hub for help.
